title: 28-Layer Stack with Thin-Layer Stochastic Perturbation
scientific_hypothesis: Layers below 70 nm thickness are numerically sensitive and contribute to convergence ceilings; applying ±15% uniform random perturbation exclusively to these thin layers while relaxing tightest_margin by 0.02 will expand the valid candidate pool and enable escape from local optima observed in iterations 07, 11, and 14.
design_principle: Targeted stochastic perturbation of thin layers disrupts numerical convergence without destabilizing the overall stack structure. Temporary margin relaxation increases valid candidate count for exploration before re-tightening.
proposed_topology: 28-layer alternating stack: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2 on fused silica substrate, air incidence
design_variables: layer thicknesses with ±15% perturbation applied to layers <70 nm from iteration_14 best candidate
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: thin layers <70 nm may require precise deposition control
outermost SiO2 layer for environmental durability
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance bands
Thin-layer sensitivity in TMM numerical computation
expected_advantages: Breaks numerical convergence ceiling observed in prior iterations
Expands valid candidate pool via margin relaxation
Preserves proven 28-layer topology while introducing controlled variation
known_risks: Margin relaxation may admit physically marginal designs
execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2. Initialize thicknesses from iteration_14 best candidate (candidate HfO2_SiO2_28layer_opt__gradient_thickness__01). Apply ±15% uniform random perturbation exclusively to layers with thickness <70 nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized. Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Temporarily relax tightest_margin constraint by 0.02 to target valid_candidates >= 15. Total layer count fixed at 28. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Changed from iteration_14 by applying feedback directive: targeted ±15% perturbation to thin layers (<70 nm) and temporary 0.02 margin relaxation. Prior iteration used Gaussian initialization without thin-layer-specific perturbation. This addresses numerical convergence issues observed in iterations 03, 11, and 14.
